title: Iraqw Goat and Roots Stew
localName: Mchuzi wa Mbuzi na Mizizi — Waaraqw
community: Iraqw people of the Mbulu Highlands — highland goat and root crop stew
author: Mama Salima
desc: Iraqw Goat and Roots Stew — goat slow-cooked with yams, turnips, and local roots in the Iraqw tradition of the Mbulu Highlands. A highland stew of great depth — the goat provides protein and bone broth, the roots provide starch and sweetness, and the altitude provides a natural pressure that makes everything more tender.
longDesc: Iraqw goat and root stew is a highland dish made for the cool evenings of the Mbulu plateau — the combination of goat (the Iraqw's primary meat animal) with the root crops that grow well at altitude produces a deeply nourishing, warming meal.
steps: Brown goat in a dry pot (no oil — the fat from the goat is sufficient).
Simmer covered on very low heat for 60 minutes.
Add root vegetables. Simmer 25—30 more minutes until everything is very tender.
chefTips: The Iraqw cook without oil — the goat's own fat renders out to cook the onions.
The root vegetables should be falling-soft.
cookingScience: See TZA024 for goat stew cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Iraqw goat herding is well-adapted to the Mbulu Highlands ecology.
healthBenefits: Root vegetables provide complex carbohydrate and vitamins.
High collagen broth from bone-in goat.
culturalNote: Iraqw goat stew is the highland evening meal — cooked as the cool air descends from the Mbulu escarpment, eaten as a family around the fire. The Iraqw's Cushitic heritage is reflected in their emphasis on goat over cattle — the same preference found across the Horn of Africa.
